expectations.text: Rejects the server-computed request-body hash as the dedup key and requires a client-minted idempotency key (e.g. an Idempotency-Key header)
expectations.evidence: "I recommend **not** building the SHA-256-body-as-key design"; "Header: `Idempotency-Key`, minted by the client and never derived by the server."

expectations.text: Justifies the rejection with the intentional-duplicate case: two genuinely identical transfers both intended are indistinguishable to a server-side hash, so only a caller-provided key expresses intent
expectations.evidence: "Two identical transfers (same vendor, same amount) in one day have identical bodies... Only the client knows whether a request is a retry or a new intent."

expectations.text: Rejects the single global dedup table and scopes uniqueness per caller as (account_id, idempotency_key)
expectations.evidence: "A global table leaks across tenants... Scope must be `(account_id, key)`."

expectations.text: Recommends event-derived key derivation as the default (a key built from an identifier the caller already holds, e.g. their own transfer or order id)
expectations.evidence: "Best: derive it from your own business identifier... This is the default recommendation."

expectations.text: Presents derivation options as a ranking - event-derived over request-scoped over a random UUID reused across retries - not an unordered list
expectations.evidence: Best: business identifier; "If no stable ID exists": request-scoped; "If you're a stateless script": random UUID persisted.

expectations.text: Names a fresh key value generated per attempt (regenerated UUID or timestamp) as the anti-pattern that defeats the mechanism, not as a fourth ranked option
expectations.evidence: "Don't: Generate a new key per attempt (`Date.now()`, a fresh `randomUUID()` in the retry loop). That defeats the protection."

expectations.text: Specifies that the same key arriving with a different request body is rejected with a conflict (409), never silently replayed
expectations.evidence: "`409` with code `invalid_idempotent_request`."

expectations.text: Recommends storing a payload fingerprint or checksum beside the key to enforce the mismatch guard
expectations.evidence: "request_fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL"; "SHA-256 of the canonicalized body, stored with the key."

expectations.text: Stores failed outcomes as well as successes so a retry replays the original result
expectations.evidence: "Stored outcomes: both successes and failures, replayed verbatim"

expectations.text: Makes or demands an explicit decision whether a stored failure replays verbatim or the operation is re-attempted without side effects (the Stripe v1 vs v2 fork)
expectations.evidence: "Failure policy (decided, not left open): a stored terminal result replays verbatim, including 4xx."

expectations.text: Does not treat the Idempotency-Key header as a ratified standard - notes the IETF draft expired unratified, so TTL, mismatch and concurrency semantics must be explicitly designed and documented
expectations.evidence: No mention of the IETF draft or the absence of a ratified standard anywhere in the transcript.
